title: Field notes: ask mapping + solution hypotheses (compact)
content:
Purpose:
A compact, field-centric synthesis of customer asks collected Jan–Mar 2026. Goal: map asks to product surfaces, propose pragmatic solution hypotheses, estimate relative effort, and nominate owners for a quick prioritization meeting. This is a working note (not exhaustive).

Method & scope:
- Sources: 12 enterprise discovery calls, 7 post-pilot survey responses, three support threads, two solutions-eng engagements (notes stitched together).
- Focus areas called out repeatedly: routing/fallback policies, per-route cost visibility, private deployment onboarding friction, granular rollouts (canaries + failovers), batch/kv-cache tuning presets, and improved error diagnostics for streaming sessions.
- Conservative filter: included asks mentioned by at least two distinct customers or flagged as high-impact by a CS lead.

Top themes (summary):
1) Predictable routing & graceful degradation (high impact, cross-team)
   - Ask: formal policy builder to route by latency SLO, cost tier, or region with automatic fallback to compatible model variants. Customers want clear precedence rules and visibility when fallbacks occur.
   - Pain: opaque behavior in multi-model setups; surprises during peak load or region outages.
2) Per-route token cost & estimated bill preview (high impact, quick win)
   - Ask: show token cost estimates per route/endpoint and predict monthly spend given current traffic. Team asks for an API + console view.
   - Pain: engineering and finance struggle to forecast and allocate spend by product feature.
3) Private onboarding checklist + self-serve diagnostics (medium-high impact, medium effort)
   - Ask: templated network checklist, automated connectivity checks for VPC, and a diagnostic bundle that customers can run pre-onboarding.
   - Pain: long setup calls and finger-pointing across infra teams.
4) Canary/targeted rollouts with rollback metrics (medium impact)
   - Ask: route percentage-based traffic, match by user segments, and automatic rollback on quality regressions (prompt set-based triggers).
   - Pain: manual rollouts lack safe signals; teams revert to heavy shadowing.
5) Out-of-the-box performance presets (batching + cache) (medium impact, low effort)
   - Ask: workload templates for chat vs. completion vs. embedding workloads that wire batching and KV-cache params.
   - Pain: customers tune by trial-and-error, risking higher costs or latency regressions.
6) Streaming + error observability (medium impact)
   - Ask: richer streaming error codes, correlation ids surfaced to the app layer, and per-token failure traces in traces/console.
   - Pain: customers can’t debug partial outputs or intermittent token stalls quickly.

Representative asks (condensed):
- "Give us an API to say: prefer-region=eu, fallback-region=us, max-latency=200ms; if above, route to cheaper model" (Enterprise analytics platform).
- "Show estimated cost per endpoint for the last 30 days and a forecast if traffic grows 2x" (Marketplace startup).
- "A checklist so our infra team can validate VPC peering and routing before a kickoff call" (Healthcare customer).
- "Canaries that auto-revert if hallucination rate on a fixed prompt set increases by 15%" (Fintech).
- "Presets: Realtime-chat (p99 <120ms, batching=conservative, kv-cache=enabled), Async-embed (maximize throughput)" (Product team).

Proposed solution hypotheses (prioritized for quick value):
A) Cost-preview per route (effort: small)
   - Minimum: console + per-route daily estimate computed from token counts * model rate card. Expose API for export to billing systems.
   - Rationale: high ROI for customers who asked and relatively straightforward backend aggregation.
B) Routing policy UI + lightweight policy DSL (effort: medium)
   - MVP: allow customers to declare ordered fallback chains (model/region/tier). Runtime logs an event when fallback used. DSL example: "route(priority=[region:eu, model:XXQ], fallback=[model:small-lat, region:us])".
   - Rationale: solves major trust problem; mitigates outages without full automation.
C) Private onboarding diagnostic runner (effort: medium)
   - Deliverable: one-click diagnostic bundle that runs network checks, port reachability, cert validation, and produces a shareable report for CS and SREs.
   - Rationale: reduces kickoff time and escalations; matches friction repeatedly reported.
D) Preset profiles for common workloads (effort: small)
   - Deliverable: 3 UI presets + API values for batching, cache, and quantization hints. Include guidance on cost/latency tradeoffs.
E) Canary automation tied to eval prompt sets (effort: medium-large)
   - Deliverable: canary config that measures defined metrics on golden prompts and automates rollback/fallback.

Quick impact / effort matrix (verbal):
- Low effort / High impact: Cost-preview per route; Preset profiles.
- Medium effort / High impact: Routing policy UI (MVP that logs fallbacks).
- Medium / Medium impact: Private onboarding diagnostics.
- Medium-high / High impact: Canary automation (needs eval infra + metric definitions).

Open questions & risks:
- Billing accuracy: do we use list-rate or negotiated customer rate for per-route preview? (finance input needed).
- Security: what diagnostic data is safe to share from customer networks? Need compliance sign-off for the diagnostic bundle.
- SLA interactions: if routing policy moves traffic to cheaper models, how are latency/quality SLAs reported to customers? Potential for disputes.
- Data retention: logs of fallback events may be PI-sensitive — decide retention policy.

Suggested immediate next steps (owner proposals):
- 1) Run a 30-minute prioritization sync (CS, Product-hosted-api, Eng-serving-runtime) — nominate Marceline and Priya to run. (Owner: Marceline Cho)
- 2) Ship a one-pager for cost-preview (scope + acceptance criteria) and get finance to confirm rate choice. (Owner: Ethan Romero)
- 3) Build prototype fallback-logging in runtime (Eng-serving-runtime spike) and wire event to console as a log. (Owner: Eng-serving-runtime lead — tag: JIRA-CS-3789)
- 4) Draft private-deploy diagnostic checklist and share with 2 recent pilot customers for validation. (Owner: Liam O'Connor)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally compact; if the group wants, I can expand into a detailed PRD for the top 2 items (cost-preview and routing policy).
- Please flag any additional customer threads that should be included (I omitted single-mention asks unless they were unusually high-value).

Appendix (quick verbatim snippets):
- "We get surprised charges because everything funnels to a single platform bill — we need per-feature breakout." — PM, marketplace startup.
- "During the last region failover our app saw a quiet routing change; we want to understand automatic fallbacks before they happen." — infra lead, enterprise.
- "If you give us a diagnostic runner we can resolve 60% of our pre-kickoff issues without CS calls." — solutions eng contact at healthcare customer.

End of note.
